slides.text: The 7:15 AM subway train was always packed, but we somehow managed to carve out our own silent, electric universe. For two years, we stood on opposite sides of the carriage. He was an exhausted medical resident; I was an anxious copywriter. We never actually spoke. We just traded tired smiles, mutual eye rolls when the train stalled, and deep, lingering glances that made my stomach do absolute backflips.

Then, my company announced an immediate relocation. Friday was my very last day on the 7:15 train. I was utterly heartbroken, realizing I would never see my beautiful train stranger again. As the subway screeched toward my final stop, I desperately grabbed a pen and scribbled my phone number on the back of my coffee receipt. My hands shook violently as I pushed through the dense crowd to reach him.

Just as I opened my mouth to speak, he held up a small, folded piece of paper. He had pushed through the thick crowd too. We breathlessly traded our scraps of paper as the doors slid open. On the cold platform, I unfolded his note. It wasn't just a phone number. It read in messy handwriting: 'I've been madly in love with you since 86th Street. Please don't let this be our last stop.'
